subject: read stan-csv files from variational inference with rstan

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: read stan-csv files from variational inference with rstan
parts:
Hello,

in Rstan the command read_stan_csv cannot read stan-csv files that were created by cmdstan 
when variational inference/advi was used (because some variables written during HMC estimation
are not written during advi estimation).

Would it be possible to modify read_stan_csv so that it can also read cmdstan csv files generated from advi
estimation?

Best - Guido

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: read stan-csv files from variational inference with rstan
parts:
On Monday, December 7, 2015 at 6:06:56 AM UTC-5, Guido Biele wrote:
Would it be possible to modify read_stan_csv so that it can also read cmdstan csv files generated from advi
estimation?

Not easily, due to the irregularities in the csv files produced by MCMC. We ended up writing an entirely separate CSV reader for ADVI called read_one_stan_csv that you can download from GitHub. By itself, it does not create a stanfit object, but there is not much to do with the ADVI output except calculate means and stuff.

Ben

parts:
Thanks Ben!

I wanted to use the advi output to do posterior predictive checks etc. As I had already set up a workflow for stanfit objects, I had hoped I could use the same workflow for advi output....
Am I wrong in assuming that I can do all "post estimation" steps I used for HMC estimation also for advi estimation?

Totally unrelated, but maybe of interest to you, Ben: The steps for installing stan/rstan 2.8.9 you described on the dev list did not work for me under windows.
- the submodules for stan and the math library were not downloaded when using install_git to install StanHeaders (I just downloaded them manually and put them into the right folder, but this is not optimal ...)
- when installing rstan with install_github the flag "branch" is used. "branch" works for install_git, but not for install_github, where "ref = "develop"" needs to be used).


Best  - guido

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: read stan-csv files from variational inference with rstan
parts:
On Monday, December 7, 2015 at 11:07:23 AM UTC-5, Guido Biele wrote:
I wanted to use the advi output to do posterior predictive checks etc. As I had already set up a workflow for stanfit objects, I had hoped I could use the same workflow for advi output....
Am I wrong in assuming that I can do all "post estimation" steps I used for HMC estimation also for advi estimation?

Posterior predictive checks you can do, but if those don't look good it may be due to the variational approximation to the posterior distribution than the posterior distribution itself. All the checks involving r_hat, n_eff, divergent transitions, hitting the maximum treedepth, MCMC standard error calculations, etc. are currently not applicable to ADVI.

Totally unrelated, but maybe of interest to you, Ben: The steps for installing stan/rstan 2.8.9 you described on the dev list did not work for me under windows.
- the submodules for stan and the math library were not downloaded when using install_git to install StanHeaders (I just downloaded them manually and put them into the right folder, but this is not optimal ...)
- when installing rstan with install_github the flag "branch" is used. "branch" works for install_git, but not for install_github, where "ref = "develop"" needs to be used).

OK, hopefully fixed now.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] read stan-csv files from variational inference with rstan
parts:
There's no reason in principle these can't be portable,
so I created a feature request citing Guido and Ben:

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues/239

We'll work on it during the refactoring --- that should
probably take care of this as a side effect if we keep all
our ducks in a row.

- Bob
